step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Visual Analysis: The diagram shows an external Healthcare entity on the left (ThirdParty) sending data into an AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB). The NLB forwards traffic to an HAProxy Ingress Controller running on an EC2 instance within an EKS cluster boundary. This routes to an App container running on a second EC2 instance (m6g Graviton). The App EC2 instance connects to an encrypted EBS (gp3) storage volume and forwards transformed healthcare data to a destination Healthcare entity (ThirdParty) on the right. In parallel, container images from Amazon ECR are deployed to the app workload instances in EKS.
2. Service Mapping: Extracted services include ThirdParty (Healthcare Source and Destination), NLB, EC2 (HAProxy), EC2 (App), EBS, EKS, and ECR.
3. Flow Sequencing: Flow 0 traces the data processing path from Healthcare Source -> NLB -> HAProxy EC2 -> App EC2 -> EBS / Healthcare Destination. Flow 1 traces deployment of container images from ECR to the application EC2 instances.
